transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-05 16:00 UTC | Duration: 58m | Recording: Yes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Riley Gomez (Redwood SE), Samantha Lee (DatumWorks - Head of ML Ops), Carlos Mendez (DatumWorks - Platform Eng), Priya Shah (DatumWorks - Dir Product), Ethan Wu (DatumWorks - Security)

00:00 Jordan: Alright, thanks everyone for joining — we wanted to use today to lock the acceptance test plan for the trial, make sure the go/no-go thresholds are clear, and agree on the schedule for running the benchmarks. Uh — quick intro round if someone new on the line.
00:17 Samantha: Hi yes Samantha here, we run infra and ML ops for DatumWorks. Short on time today so we'll try to move through the checklist.
00:22 Priya: Priya here, product lead, mostly interested in user-facing latency and the quality regression numbers.
00:28 Jordan: Great. Riley, quick outline?
00:30 Riley: Yeah — plan is simple: we propose three workloads, each with an objective metric set — latency p95, throughput, cost per 1k tokens, and a quality pass metric (F1 or rubric-based accuracy depending on workload). We'll run in Redwood-hosted sandbox first, then optional private run if you want to test VPC and KMS behavior.
00:50 Carlos: Question — how do you measure quality? Are you using human labels or automated evals?
00:55 Riley: Good question. For each workload we'll accept two forms: (1) automated metric (e.g., BLEU, ROUGE, F1) on your labeled holdout OR (2) a small human eval set — either way we translate it to a pass threshold. Example: classification workload must be >= 92% F1 on the holdout for pass.
01:12 Samantha: 92 F1 seems high for our noisy data. Can we instead say relative regression tolerance, like no more than 3% drop versus our baseline model?
01:20 Jordan: Absolutely — we typically allow either an absolute threshold or delta against your baseline. We should capture both so the report is unambiguous.
01:28 Priya: Also need to capture inference tail latencies for interactive flows — p95 and p99. p99 is critical for UX.
01:35 Riley: We'll record p50/p95/p99 and show token-level latency and end-to-end. Also we'll show KV cache warm vs cold behavior because your use case has repeated context.
01:46 Ethan: Quick security note — for private runs we need to validate KMS integration, audit log export, and SSO access. Can you provide the list of artifacts you'll need?
01:54 Jordan: Yes, we'll send a security checklist. For the hosted benchmark we can obfuscate data but for the private run we'll need KMS config and a service account with least privilege.
02:06 Carlos: On sizing — for throughput we normally see 300 concurrent requests at peak, about 8 tokens average response length, ~1000 requests per minute sustained. Is that enough detail?
02:19 Riley: That's perfect. For the benchmark we'll simulate that mix and also run a high-concurrency burst to test autoscaling behavior. We'll capture latency SLO violations and tail latency during bursts.
02:32 Samantha: Timelines? We want results before our steering committee on 2026-04-01. Is that realistic?
02:38 Jordan: Yes if we start the benchmark mid-March. Proposal: you supply workloads by 2026-03-10, we do setup and a dry run the week of 2026-03-16, then two full weeks of automated runs 2026-03-23 to 2026-04-05, with final report delivered 2026-04-07. That gets you the summary before 4/1? Actually final report 4/7 would be after 4/1 — we can compress.
03:00 Priya: We need an executive summary by 2026-03-30 for the steering committee — even if the full report is later.
03:06 Jordan: Fair. We'll deliver an interim exec summary by 2026-03-30 with preliminary pass/fail flags; full detailed report by 2026-04-07.
03:14 Samantha: Sounds good. Now on go/no-go thresholds — list them out.
03:18 Riley: Proposed pass criteria per workload: (A) Latency: p95 <= 250ms for interactive workload, p99 <= 600ms; (B) Throughput: sustain 1k rpm with <1% error rate and <5% SLO violations; (C) Quality: either absolute metric or delta <= -3% vs baseline; (D) Cost: at agreed target cost-per-1k tokens or within 15% of our cost model. Any of these failing triggers a no-go unless mitigations agreed.
03:42 Carlos: About the cost threshold — our finance wants a hard cost ceiling rather than percent. Can we put both?
03:48 Jordan: We'll include both: absolute ceiling you specify in the template and relative compare to your baseline cost.
03:55 Ethan: Clarify the remediation path — if latency fails but quality is great, do we still call it no-go?
04:01 Riley: We'll define severity levels in the report: Critical failure (major SLO and security breaches) = no-go; Major failure (one or two core metrics breach beyond tolerance) = conditional with remediation plan; Minor = pass with notes. The final decision belongs to DatumWorks steering committee using the report.
04:18 Samantha: OK documented. What about reporting format? We prefer a spreadsheet + short PDF executive summary and raw logs for SE analysis.
04:27 Jordan: That's our standard: CSV of raw traces, a dashboard link (Grafana snapshot), a templated spreadsheet with pass/fail cells, and a one-page PDF exec summary with recommendation. We'll also attach a runbook with commands to reproduce.
04:40 Priya: For reproducibility please include seed, model version, tokenization and quantization flags in the report.
04:45 Riley: Absolutely — we'll include the exact model hash, Redwood runtime kernel selection notes, batch sizes, quantization level, and seed. Note — sometimes the auto transcriber writes 'kv cache' as K V cash — sorry, speaking fast.
04:58 Samantha: Ha — noted. On measurement — can you guarantee identical hardware between runs?
05:03 Riley: For hosted sandbox we'll run on a consistent instance type but don't promise exact GPU SKU parity unless you run private/dedicated. We can provide both: hosted run for quick results; dedicated pool run for production parity.
05:16 Carlos: For the private run we will test on our dedicated infra — can Redwood run the same harness inside our VPC?
05:22 Jordan: Yes, Redwood Private supports a VPC deployment and we can orchestrate runs there. There will be a separate checklist for connectivity, KMS, and logs.
05:31 Ethan: Also need to validate audit logging retention and whether logs can be forwarded to our SIEM.
05:36 Riley: We support syslog/S3 exports and can forward to Splunk/Datadog — we'll document retention and endpoints.
05:44 Priya: What about model fallbacks — if the primary model exceeds latency, will Redwood automatically route to a lower-latency variant?
05:51 Jordan: Smart routing is configurable; for the trial we can run deterministic runs without fallback so you measure worst-case. But we can also run an additional scenario with routing policy to show graceful degradation.
06:03 Samantha: Good. On the benchmark template — show a row for each workload and columns: baseline metrics, trial metrics, delta, pass/fail, notes.
06:13 Riley: Yep that's the exact template we'll send. Also we'll include plots: latency percentile graphs, cost breakdown, per-token cost and heatmap of SLO violations over time.
06:24 Carlos: Any automation for generating the report? We prefer a reproducible pipeline.
06:28 Riley: We'll provide a reproducible harness (python scripts + Dockerfile) that runs the three workloads and spits out the CSVs and Grafana snapshots. SE-runbook will be included.
06:38 Samantha: Ok. There was mention of human evals earlier — they take time and budget. Can we limit to 200 samples per workload?
06:44 Riley: 200 is fine for spot checks — though if you want more robust significance we can do bootstrap sampling and provide confidence intervals.
06:52 Priya: We need to see confidence intervals on quality metrics in the report.
06:56 Riley: We'll include 95% CIs where applicable.
07:00 Samantha: Any dependencies from our side?
07:04 Jordan: We need: (1) sample datasets and baseline model outputs, (2) acceptance baseline metrics, (3) security artifacts for private runs, (4) a contact person for infra and for product decisions.
07:18 Samantha: That will be me for infra and Priya for product.
07:22 Jordan: Great. Quick readback of dates — Jordan to send template by 3/6, Samantha to provide workloads by 3/10, Riley to propose exact slots for dry run week of 3/16, full runs 3/23-4/05, interim exec summary 3/30, final report 4/07. Any objections?
07:45 Priya: Works.
07:47 Ethan: Works.
07:48 Carlos: Works on our end.
07:50 Jordan: Perfect. Final few items — scoring rubric language for the pass/fail cells. We'll provide three states: PASS, CONDITIONAL PASS, FAIL. Conditional lists remediation actions and target re-run windows.
08:03 Riley: Also capturing systemic risk items: security non-compliance => immediate no-go; major data leakage => immediate stop.
08:12 Samantha: Agree. Also please include an appendix that maps each metric to a business question — e.g., p99 latency -> conversion rate impact, cost-per-1k -> monthly opex.
08:26 Jordan: We'll include that mapping. Anything else?
08:30 Priya: A short note on sample representativeness — we might forward a few production logs with PII redacted.
08:36 Ethan: Also confirm we can run the private deployment behind our proxy — we will provide proxy details if needed.
08:41 Riley: Noted.
08:43 Jordan: Ok let's summarize next steps — (reads from checklist) Jordan send benchmark template & report example, Riley send harness and preliminary runbook, DatumWorks provide workloads and security artifacts. We'll reconvene after the dry run to look at preliminary metrics.
08:58 Samantha: Thanks everyone. Look for the template.
09:01 Jordan: Thanks all. Closing.
